newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends shy of record as oil stocks spurt higher.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends shy of record as oil stocks spurt higher.

text.p: The Dow industrials were thrust closer to record territory on a renewed rally by oil stocks, with market sentiment aided by a Federal Reserve report that there was no clear sign of higher inflation.

"The Dow would be flat if it weren't for oil stocks. Demand is strong and the Iraqi situation is just frosting on the cake," said Jack Shaughnessy, director of research at Advest. NYMEX October crude climbed $0.63 to $24.75 a barrel as U.S.-Iraqi tensions mounted.
The Dow rose 28 points to about 5755.
That left the blue chip index just shy of its record closing high of 5778.00, reached May 22.
More than half of the Dow's gain came from strength in Chevron, up 1-1/8 to 61-1/2, Texaco, up 1-7/8 to 94-5/8, Exxon, up 1-3/8 to 84-3/4, and Conoco's parent Du Pont, up one to 85-1/4.

Stocks reversed morning losses with bonds after the Fed's Beige Book economic survey noted greater upward pressures on wages than prices but called inflation signs "inconclusive." As expected, the Fed said U.S. business activity was good and expanding moderately.
The report was based on information collected before September 4 in the 12 Fed districts and will be used when central bank policymakers meet on September 24 to plot interest-rate strategy.

"The bounce in the market is closely tied to the Beige Book. There was relief it was not stronger than it was, and now people are back to thinking a 25-basis-point tightening or no change," said Michael LaTronica, Gruntal director of research.
Value Line Asset Management chief investment officer Phil Orlando said, "We'll have a much better reading on inflation and whether the Fed will raise rates after PPI and CPI."

August producer prices, scheduled for Thursday, are expected to be up 0.1 percent for both overall and core prices, which exclude food and energy. Consumer prices, due Friday, are seen up 0.2 percent both overall and core.
"We want to see Thursday and Friday's numbers, but the consensus is we're on a pace for a 2.7 percent CPI-base inflation for the year which is pretty benign," LaTronica said.

Technology stocks were mostly stronger despite another quarterly earnings warning from Motorola Inc. Shares of the chip and cell-phone maker, the most heavily traded on the NYSE, lost 1-5/8 to 49. The Nasdaq Composite rose five to 1154.
On the NYSE, gainers beat losers 6-5 on active volume of about 373 million shares.
The long bond slipped 1/32 to yield 7.11 percent after afternoon news that the Chicago Fed manufacturing index rose 0.5 percent for July to a record high of 128.9.

Stocks got a lift after the Investment Company Institute estimated new flows into stock funds were $19.0 billion in August, a jump from July's $5.8 billion and a return to the record pace of earlier in 1996. "Don't run away from stocks. There's plenty of money to buy them up regardless of who wins the election," said Ken Ducey, BT Brokerage's head of trading.
Among individual stocks, silicon wafer manufacturer MEMC Electronic Materials Inc dropped 8-1/2 to 20-3/4 after warning of shortfalls in third- and fourth-quarter sales.
Itron Inc lost eight to 21 after the maker of data acquisition and wireless communication products for meter reading warned results would fall short of expectations.

Eli Lilly rose one to 60-3/8. Salomon Brothers upgraded the stock to strong buy from buy on expectations that worldwide approvals and introductions of Zyprexa, a new therapy for schizophrenia, were imminent.
Premenos Technology Corp climbed 4-5/8 to 16-3/4.
AT&T Corp will license software developed by Premenos that allows customers to trade information with other companies over the Internet. AT&T rose 1-3/8 to 55.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 4.52 to 1153.95.
The S&P 500 index rose 3.47 to 667.28.
(Figures official as of 1645 EDT/2045 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk, 212 859-1721
